content:
maria: Heads-up — privatelink endpoint in us-west-2 failing to assume service role, audit logs not reaching Splunk, blocking node provisioning for gpu-pool-3.

jamal: Is this the same error we saw last month? any logs?

maria: I see IAM:AccessDenied when sts:AssumeRole from vpce-service-0a1b2c. KMS audit shows no PutObject to s3-logs bucket. GPU nodes stuck in provisioning step 'attach-network-interfaces'

ops-bot: Alert: VPC Endpoint privatelink-usw2 returned 403 for role-assume on 1764447777

sre-jen: tl;dr: privatelink policy denies principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-vpce-service-role

alex: Any terraform change recently? maybe role path changed

maria: No infra terraform PRs merged in last 24h for vpce or roles. IAM console shows role exists but trust policy was replaced by automation earlier today.

security-tim: I pushed a scoped trust change to reduce broad sts:AssumeRole — probably too strict. Reverting now unless objections.

jamal: Please paste the trust policy diff

security-tim: Diff: removed "Service": "vpce.amazonaws.com" and added explicit principal account list. Ops needs principal for privatelink service account.

maria: That's the problem. We need service principal for privatelink: {"Service":"vpce.amazonaws.com"} or the specific VPCE service principal arn. Current role assume fails until we revert.

sre-jen: Workaround: attach temporary inline policy to provisioning role to allow ec2:AttachNetworkInterface and kms:Decrypt? but trust still needed for assume role.

alex: Can we fallback provisioning to public subnet while we fix? That would increase cross-AZ egress and cost — estimate +$1200/day for burst nodes.

maria: Prefer not; some projects require private-only. Also audit/compliance prohibits falling back for these customers.

ops-bot: Runbook step suggested: revert trust policy -> restart vpce service to re-evaluate. Command: aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name infra-vpce-service-role --policy-document file://trust.json

jamal: I'll prepare the revert PR and set a 2-minute maintenance window. tagging @security-tim for approval.

security-tim: Approve for emergency revert. I'll monitor logs and keep retention markers.

maria: After revert we should rehydrate S3 audit logs. Current evidence: s3 list shows gap from 2026-02-18T04:00Z to 2026-02-18T06:45Z.

sre-jen: Monitoring: healthcheck for gpu-pool-3 hit 502s; kubectl shows pods stuck CrashLoopBackOff on network-attach. Logs:

maria: ```
Error attaching ENI: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/infra-vpce-service-role/vpce-attach is not authorized to perform: ec2:AttachNetworkInterface
```

jamal: After revert, I'll trigger reprovision for 4 nodes in gpu-pool-3. ops-bot, please hold autoscale from adding more nodes until we confirm.

ops-bot: Action: autoscaler paused for gpu-pool-3 by @jamal; timestamp 1764447900

security-tim: I'll also run a least-privilege review post-mitigation to avoid recurring drift.

alex: Any permanent fix ideas? Maybe test harness that validates trust policy before automation deploys.

maria: Yes. Proposal: CI job that runs 'aws iam simulate-principal-policy' and 'sts:assumeRole' test with a dry-run for every role change PR. Plus alert on audit log gaps.

jamal: I'll open a ticket: INFRA-4527 with remediation steps and cost impact. Assign to eng-infra and secops.

maria: Thanks. Next steps: jamal revert PR in 5, monitor logs, re-provision nodes, confirm KMS audit arrives in Splunk, update runbook.

sre-jen: :thumbsup:
